title: All Unitaries Have Constant Depth Quantum Circuits
abstract: It is well-known that every $n$-qubit unitary can be implemented by a $2^{O(n)}$-depth quantum circuit using single- and two-qubit gates. It has been open whether exponential depth is \emph{necessary} for general unitaries, even when allowing for unlimited number of ancilla qubits. We show, perhaps surprisingly, that all unitaries can be approximated to operator norm $ε$ by a circuit of one- and two-qubit gates of depth $\poly(n,\log 1/ε)$ with $2^{O(n)}$ ancilla qubits. In other words, every $n$-qubit unitary can be parallelized to polynomial depth. Moreover, if we allow unbounded fan-out gates, these circuits can be reduced further to \emph{constant} depth. Our construction takes advantage of a novel relationship connecting the unitary synthesis problem of Aaronson and Kuperberg to locally-decodable codes and private information retrieval from complexity theory and cryptography.

bite.hook: Any n-qubit unitary can be compressed to constant circuit depth using unbounded fan-out gates and 2^O(n) ancillas.
tldr: Investigated whether arbitrary n-qubit quantum operations inherently require exponential circuit execution time.
Connected unitary synthesis to error-correcting codes and private information retrieval from theoretical computer science.
Proved all unitaries can run in polynomial depth, or constant depth if unbounded fan-out operations are available.
bite.whyItMatters: This resolves a longstanding open question about parallel quantum computation by showing that extreme circuit depth is never strictly required if enough auxiliary qubits are available.
bite.eli5: Imagine a massive calculation that usually takes billions of sequential steps. This result proves you can recruit a huge army of helper notepads to do almost everything at once, finishing the entire task in constant time.
